parsed.title: Zhang's prescribed-vertex complementary cycle conjecture for regular bipartite tournaments
parsed.statement:
Let $D$ be a $k$-regular bipartite tournament, where $k$ is an integer greater than $2$, and let $u$ and $v$ be two specified vertices of $D$. Let $F_{4k}$ and the other specified exceptional families be the digraphs excluded below. **Zhang and collaborators' conjecture.** If $D$ is isomorphic to neither $F_{4k}$ nor any of the other specified families of digraphs, then for every even $p$ satisfying

$$
4\leq p\leq |V(D)|-4,
$$

$D$ has a cycle $C$ of length $p$ such that $D\setminus C$ is hamiltonian, $C$ contains $u$, and $D\setminus C$ contains $v$. This conjecture prescribes one vertex on the selected cycle and another on its hamiltonian complement; its status is not resolved in the supplied source.
parsed.source_name: Stéphane Bessy and Jocelyn Thiebaut, “Complementary cycles of any length in regular bipartite tournaments”, arXiv:2102.04514 (2021).

parsed.title: Complementary cycle-factor conjecture for fully regular multipartite tournaments
parsed.statement:
Let $D$ be a $k$-fully regular $c$-partite tournament with $c\geq5$, meaning that for every pair of distinct partite sets, their induced bipartite tournament is $k$-regular. A **$(p,|V(D)|-p)$-cycle-factor** is a cycle-factor consisting of cycles of lengths $p$ and $|V(D)|-p$. **Fully regular complementary cycle-factor conjecture.** For every even $p$ satisfying

$$
4\leq p\leq |V(D)|-4,
$$

$D$ has a $(p,|V(D)|-p)$-cycle-factor. This is presented as an extension of the paper's results and as a weaker form of Yeo's conjecture; no resolution is supplied.
parsed.source_name: Stéphane Bessy and Jocelyn Thiebaut, “Complementary cycles of any length in regular bipartite tournaments”, arXiv:2102.04514 (2021).

parsed.title: Valuation characterization of generic bipartite rigidity matroids
parsed.statement:
Let $K_{m,n}$ be a complete bipartite graph, and let $\mathcal R^{k,\ell}_{m,n}$ be the generic $(k,\ell)$-rigidity matroid, whose rank is $\ell m+kn-k\ell$. A rooted $K_{k+1,\ell+1}$-sequence is a rooted sequence of copies of $K_{k+1,\ell+1}$ in $K_{m,n}$, and $\operatorname{val}(F,\mathcal S)$ denotes the associated valuation. **Bipartite rigidity conjecture.** The matroid $\mathcal R^{k,\ell}_{m,n}$ is the unique maximal rooted $K_{k+1,\ell+1}$-matroid on $K_{m,n}$, and for every $F\subseteq E(K_{n,m})$ its rank is

$$
r(F)=\min\{\operatorname{val}(F,\mathcal S):\mathcal S\text{ is a proper, rooted }K_{k+1,\ell+1}\text{-sequence in }K_{m,n}\}.
$$

The statement extends the proved case $\ell=1$; the general case $k,\ell\geq1$ remains open.
parsed.source_name: Bill Jackson and Shin-ichi Tanigawa, “Maximal Matroids in Weak Order Posets”, arXiv:2102.09901 (2021).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.09901

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2021). “The Schwarz-Zippel Lemma implies that the problem is in the class NP, but it is a long-standing open problem to show that it is also in co-NP.”

parsed.title: The even-base min-entropy formula conjecture for entropoid power shapes
parsed.statement:
Let $\mathbb{E}_{p^2}$ be an entropoid and let $g\in\mathbb{E}^*_{(p-1)^2}$ generate its maximal multiplicative subgroupoid. For every even base $\mathfrak{b}=2b_1<b_{\max}$, let $n(\mathfrak{b},i)=\max n_{ij}$. The **even-base min-entropy conjecture.**

$$
n(\mathfrak{b},i)=(\mathfrak{b}-1)\left((\mathfrak{b}-1)^{i-1}-(\mathfrak{b}-2)^{i-1}\right),
$$

and consequently

$$
H_{\infty}(\xi_i)=1-\left(\frac{\mathfrak{b}-2}{\mathfrak{b}-1}\right)^{i-1}.
$$

The formula formalizes the observed even-versus-odd base pattern in the distribution of bracketing shapes; the paper reports it as an observed conjectural relation rather than proving it.
parsed.source_name: Danilo Gligoroski, “Entropoid Based Cryptography”, arXiv:2104.05598 (2021).

parsed.title: The generalized cross-product conjecture for posets
parsed.statement:
Let $P=(X,\prec)$ be a finite poset, let $x,y,z\in X$ be distinct, and for integers $k,\ell$ let $F(k,\ell)$ denote the number of linear extensions $L\in\operatorname{\mathcal{E}}(P)$ satisfying $L(y)-L(x)=k$ and $L(z)-L(y)=\ell$. **Generalized cross-product conjecture.** For all $i,j,k,\ell\geq 1$,

$$
F(k,\ell)F(k+i,\ell+j)\leq F(k,\ell+j)F(k+i,\ell).
$$

The paper proves an extension of this statement in its width-two setting, but presents the general assertion as a conjecture; its status beyond that setting is open.
parsed.source_name: Swee Hong Chan, Igor Pak and Greta Panova, “The cross-product conjecture for width two posets”, arXiv:2104.09009 (2022).

parsed.title: Shor's bounds for the distance-polynomial peak of trees
parsed.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree on $n$ vertices, and let $p_D(T)$ denote the index of the peak of the normalized coefficients of the characteristic polynomial of the distance matrix of $T$. **Shor's conjecture.**

$$
\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft\lfloor \frac{n}{2}\aftergroup\egroup\originalright\rfloor \leq p_D(T) \leq \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft\lceil n\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)\aftergroup\egroup\originalright\rceil.
$$

The lower and upper bounds correspond respectively to the star and the path. The source describes this as an open conjecture concerning the possible location of the distance-polynomial peak for arbitrary trees.
parsed.source_name: Adam Zsolt Wagner, “Constructions in combinatorics via neural networks”, arXiv:2104.14516 (2021).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.14516

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of April 2021). “The conjecture regarding the location of the peak was disproved by Collins who showed that for paths the peak is at index approximately $\left(1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\right)n$.”

parsed.title: Degree-two characterization conjecture for simple or cosimple connected binary matroids
parsed.statement:
Let $M$ be a connected binary matroid that is simple or cosimple. The statements (a), (b), and (c) in the degree-two lemma are equivalent. **Degree-two characterization conjecture.**

The preceding theorem proves the equivalence, with the additional condition (a$'$), for graphic and cographic matroids, while the example $F_7^*$ shows that (a$'$) need not hold for every simple and cosimple connected binary matroid. The conjecture asks whether (a), (b), and (c) alone are nevertheless equivalent in this broader class.
parsed.source_name: Tim Römer and Sara Saeedi Madani, “Cycle algebras and polytopes of matroids”, arXiv:2105.00185 (2021).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.00185

350699.raw:
{"mathdb_id": 350699, "uuid": "24368411-b5db-4257-8078-7c2bfcb6ec6a", "canonical_url": "https://mathdb.com/p/350699/bourgain-demeter-s-additive-energy-conjecture-for-the-2-sphe", "title": "Bourgain--Demeter's additive-energy conjecture for the 2-sphere", "statement": "Let $\mathcal{S}_{3,1}=\{\bm{x}\in\mathbb{R}^3:x_1^2+x_2^2+x_3^2=1\}$, and let $E_{2,2}(A)$ denote the number of quadruples $(\bm{x}_1,\bm{x}_2,\bm{x}_3,\bm{x}_4)\in A^4$ satisfying $\bm{x}_1+\bm{x}_2=\bm{x}_3+\bm{x}_4$. **Bourgain--Demeter's additive-energy conjecture.** For every finite, non-empty subset $A\subseteq\mathcal{S}_{3,1}$,

$$
E_{2,2}(A)\ll_{\epsilon}|A|^{2+\epsilon}.

parsed.title: Bourgain--Demeter's additive-energy conjecture for the 2-sphere
parsed.statement:
Let $\mathcal{S}_{3,1}=\{\bm{x}\in\mathbb{R}^3:x_1^2+x_2^2+x_3^2=1\}$, and let $E_{2,2}(A)$ denote the number of quadruples $(\bm{x}_1,\bm{x}_2,\bm{x}_3,\bm{x}_4)\in A^4$ satisfying $\bm{x}_1+\bm{x}_2=\bm{x}_3+\bm{x}_4$. **Bourgain--Demeter's additive-energy conjecture.** For every finite, non-empty subset $A\subseteq\mathcal{S}_{3,1}$,

$$
E_{2,2}(A)\ll_{\epsilon}|A|^{2+\epsilon}.
$$

This is the conjectured sharp spacing-independent bound for additive energies on the 2-sphere, analogous to the corresponding estimate for the truncated paraboloid. The paper does not state that it has been resolved.

parsed.title: Kamatchi–Arumugam characterization conjecture for distance-antimagic graphs
parsed.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let $N(u)$ denote the open neighborhood of a vertex $u$. A graph is **distance antimagic** if it admits a bijection $f:V(G)\to\{1,2,\ldots,|V(G)|\}$ such that the vertex weights

$$
w(v)=\sum_{u\in N(v)}f(u)
$$

are distinct for all vertices $v$.

**Kamatchi–Arumugam conjecture.** $G$ is distance antimagic if and only if $N(u)\ne N(v)$ for any two distinct vertices $u,v\in V(G)$.

The source says that this conjecture was put forward by Kamatchi and Arumugam and was still open at the time of the paper. It proposes a neighborhood-based characterization of distance-antimagic graphs.
parsed.source_name: Divya T and Devi Yamini S, “Local Distance Antimagic Vertex Coloring of Graphs”, arXiv:2106.01833 (2024).

parsed.title: A linear bound for the relative rank constant over finite fields
parsed.statement:
Let $d$ and $s$ be parameters, let $\mathbb F$ be a finite field with $\operatorname{char}(\mathbb F)>d$, and let $C(\mathbb F,s,d)$ denote the constant in the preceding relative-rank bound. **Linear bound conjecture.** For all finite fields $\mathbb F$ with $\operatorname{char}(\mathbb F)>d$, we have

$$
C(\mathbb F,s,d)=A(d)(1+s).
$$

This would improve the previously known bound $C=A(d)(1+s)^{B(d)}$ by making the dependence on $s$ linear. The supplied source gives no evidence that the statement has been proved or disproved.

parsed.title: The line-intersection bound conjecture for cyclic tilings
parsed.statement:
Let $A\subset\mathbb{Z}_M$, where $M=\prod_{j=1}^K p_j^{n_j}$, and suppose that $p_i^{\alpha_i}\parallel |A|$ with $\alpha_i<n_i$. Let $\ell_i(x)$ denote the line in the $p_i$ direction through $x$.

**Line-intersection bound conjecture.** For every $x\in\mathbb{Z}_M$,

$$
|A\cap\ell_i(x)|<p_i^{n_i}.
$$

parsed.title: Appendable $(e)$-positivity conjecture for labelled unit interval graphs
parsed.statement:
A labelled graph $G$ is **$(e)$-positive** if its chromatic symmetric function $y_G$ is $(e)$-positive. If $G$ and $H$ are labelled graphs, their concatenation $G+H$ is formed by identifying the final vertex of $G$ with the initial vertex of $H$. A labelled graph $H$ is **appendable $(e)$-positive** if $G+H$ is $(e)$-positive for every $(e)$-positive labelled graph $G$.

**Appendable $(e)$-positivity conjecture.** Every labelled unit interval graph is appendable $(e)$-positive.

This is explicitly described as an even more optimistic conjecture than the preceding $(e)$-positivity conjecture. The source gives no known general proof or disproof.

parsed.title: Bubble-up and missing-rim conjecture for wheels of neural codes
parsed.statement: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a neural code, let $\Delta(\mathcal{C})$ be its simplicial complex, and let $\mathcal{W}=(\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\tau)$ be a wheel of $\mathcal{C}$. A face of $\Delta(\mathcal{C})$ is a **max-intersection face** if it is the intersection of two or more facets of $\Delta(\mathcal{C})$. **Bubble-up and missing-rim conjecture.** (i) If $\mathcal{W}$ is a wheel of $\mathcal{C}$, then $\tau\notin\mathcal{C}$. The preceding results establish these properties for sprockets, wire wheels, and wheel frames; the conjecture asserts both the missing-rim and bubble-up properties for arbitrary wheels.

parsed.title: Circuit-cocircuit intersection conjecture for q-matroids
parsed.statement:
Let $M$ be a $q$-matroid with circuits $\mathcal{C}$ and cocircuits $\mathcal{C}^*$. Suppose

$$
\dim(C\cap C^*)\neq 1
$$

for all $C\in\mathcal{C}$ and $C^*\in\mathcal{C}^*$. Then Definition gives a relation on the $q$-matroid $M$.

**Circuit-cocircuit intersection conjecture.** Under these hypotheses, Definition is an equivalence relation.

This is presented as a sufficient condition suggested by the paper's examples, but the supplied text gives no evidence that it has been proved or disproved.

parsed.title: Generalized Turán inequality conjecture for plane-partition polynomials
parsed.statement:
Let $P_n(x)$ be the polynomials associated with generalized plane partitions, and define

$$
\Delta_{a,b}(x):=P_{a-1}(x)P_{b+1}(x)-P_a(x)P_b(x).
$$

Let $a$ and $b$ be integers satisfying $a-1>b\geq 0$ and $(a,b)\notin\{(4,2),(6,4)\}$. **Generalized Turán inequality conjecture.** For every real number $x\geq 2$,

$$
\Delta_{a,b}(x)>0.
$$

This generalizes the preceding Turán inequality and the Chern–Fu–Tang conjecture for $k$-colored partitions. The source provides the formulation and motivation but does not report a proof in the stated generality.
parsed.source_name: Bernhard Heim, Markus Neuhauser and Robert Tröger, “Inequalities for Plane Partitions”, arXiv:2109.15145 (2021).
